title: Fluctuation exchange study on the electron-hole asymmetry of the superconductivity across 1/3 filling in the trilayer Hubbard model
authors: Yushi Yamada, Masataka Kakoi, Masayuki Ochi, Kazuhiko Kuroki
abstract: We study within the fluctuation exchange approximation the trilayer Hubbard model where three layers of the Hubbard model are coupled by large interlayer hoppings so that the overlap of the bonding, nonbonding, and antibonding bands is relatively small. We pay special attention to the band fillings close to 1/3, for which the bonding and nonbonding bands as a whole are close to half filling. For relatively small values of the onsite $U$, superconductivity roughly exhibits electron-hole symmetric behavior, as expected for a nearly half-filled two-band system. By contrast, an asymmetry appears when $U$ becomes large, where superconductivity is more favored in the hole-doped regime, i.e., in the regime where electrons are removed from 1/3 filling. We attribute this asymmetry to the asymmetric renormalization of the bonding, nonbonding, and antibonding bands when $U$ is large.
summary: This theoretical study analyzes superconductivity in a trilayer Hubbard model near $1/3$ filling using the FLEX approximation. It finds that while weak interactions yield symmetric superconducting behavior, strong correlations induce a significant electron-hole asymmetry favoring hole doping. This suggests that spin fluctuations play a crucial role in determining the pairing symmetry and stability of the superconducting state.
main_problem: The study investigates the electron-hole asymmetry of superconductivity near $1/3$ filling in the trilayer Hubbard model.
main_result: Strong correlations (large U) induce a pronounced electron-hole asymmetry, favoring superconductivity when the system is hole-doped relative to $1/3$ filling.
method: The research employs the Fluctuation Exchange Approximation (FLEX) combined with solving the linearized Eliashberg equation to calculate superconducting parameters.
model_or_system: The model is the trilayer Hubbard model, featuring three coupled layers and an onsite interaction U. The analysis focuses on band fillings near $1/3$ where bonding and nonbonding bands are nearly half-filled.
key_observables: Superconducting coupling constant ($\lambda$), gap function ($\Delta$), spectral function ($A(\mathbf{k}, \omega)$), and dynamical spin susceptibility ($	ext{Im } \chi_s$).
important_parameters: Interaction strength ratio ($U/t_{\perp}$), doping level (hole-doped vs. electron-doped relative to $1/3$ filling).
main_assumptions: The primary approximation used is the Fluctuation Exchange Approximation (FLEX) theory, and calculations involve solving the linearized Eliashberg equation.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate $\lambda$ dependence on doping showing asymmetry for large $U/t_{\perp}$, and gap functions ($\Delta$) confirming $s_{\pm}$-wave structure in the hole-doped case versus local pairing at strong coupling.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the model and methodology (FLEX, Eliashberg), then comparing weak vs. strong coupling limits to identify the emergence of electron-hole asymmetry, and finally analyzing gap functions and spin susceptibilities across different doping regimes.
why_interesting: While focused on correlated electrons, the detailed analysis of pairing mechanisms ($\Delta$) and susceptibility ($\chi_s$) provides insights into how collective excitations (spin fluctuations) mediate pairing in strongly interacting quantum systems, which has parallels to dynamics studied in AMO physics.

FIG. 2. Band filling n dependence of the eigenvalue λ of the linearized Eliashberg equation (9) for various values of U/t⊥= 2, 4, 6 at t/t⊥= 0.25. Band filling n = 2/3 corre- sponds to 1/3-filling. Circles denote points where the anoma- lous self-energy (gap function) ∆has s-wave symmetry, while open squares denote d-wave symmetry.

Figure 2 shows the eigenvalue λ obtained by solving the linearized Eliashberg equation (9) for various U/t⊥ and the band filling n. Here, the band filling is defined as the number of electrons per site, by which n = 2/3 corre- sponds to 1/3-filling. Interestingly, while λ is symmetric about n = 2/3 for U/t⊥= 2, λ in the electron-doped region is strongly suppressed for U/t⊥= 4 and 6. This situation is reminiscent of the electron–hole asymmetry found in the three-leg ladder with strong interchain cou- pling. In the weak coupling limit, the three-leg ladder with strong interchain coupling hosts the C1S0 phase, which is favorable for superconductivity, both in electron- and hole-doped regions...
